blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how your body maintains its shape and allows you to move? The mammalian skeleton plays a crucial role in providing support, enabling movement, and protecting vital organs.

blocks.markdown: The mammalian skeleton is divided into two main parts: the axial skeleton and the appendicular skeleton. The **axial skeleton** consists of the skull, vertebral column, and rib cage, while the **appendicular skeleton** includes the bones of the limbs and girdles. Understanding these two divisions helps us appreciate how our bodies are structured.

blocks.title: Axial Skeleton
blocks.text: The axial skeleton is the central part of the skeleton, comprising the skull, vertebral column, and rib cage. It supports the head and trunk, protecting the brain and spinal cord.

blocks.markdown: The **skull** is made up of several bones, including the frontal, parietal, temporal, and occipital bones. The **vertebral column** consists of individual vertebrae that protect the spinal cord and provide flexibility. The **appendicular skeleton** includes the pectoral girdle (scapula and clavicle) and the pelvic girdle (ilium, ischium, and pubis), which connect the limbs to the trunk.

blocks.title: Identifying the Skeleton Components
blocks.prompt: List the main components of the axial and appendicular skeleton.

steps.text: 1. Identify the axial skeleton components: Skull, vertebral column, rib cage.
2. Identify the appendicular skeleton components: Pectoral girdle (scapula, clavicle) and pelvic girdle (ilium, ischium, pubis).

blocks.answer: Axial Skeleton: Skull, vertebral column, rib cage; Appendicular Skeleton: Pectoral girdle (scapula, clavicle), pelvic girdle (ilium, ischium, pubis).

blocks.markdown: The skeleton serves several important functions. It provides **support** for the body, **protection** for internal organs, enables **movement** through the attachment of muscles, and plays a role in **blood-cell formation** in the bone marrow.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: When studying the mammalian skeleton, focus on the differences between the axial and appendicular skeleton, and remember the key bones in each section. This knowledge is often tested in WAEC and NECO exams.

points: The mammalian skeleton is divided into the axial and appendicular skeleton.
The axial skeleton includes the skull and vertebral column, while the appendicular skeleton consists of limb bones and girdles.
The skeleton provides support, protection, movement, and aids in blood-cell formation.
